## TL;DR

The Cancel stalled check button flickered because a healthy heartbeat was treated as missing whenever its timestamp was slightly ahead of the card clock, and because a checks snapshot could replace a newer heartbeat with null or an older one. Stall detection now treats a small future skew as progress, the client keeps the newer valid heartbeat when snapshot and SSE disagree, and a genuinely idle check still fails closed for both the button and cancel. The selected review and engineering-report rows reserve left padding so the accent bar sits beside the pass or round number.

## Work and rationale

On a task in review the card clock that feeds stall detection does not move every time output arrives. Active engineer cards tick once a second; a review card that is not the in-flight close-out ticks every fifteen seconds. Check output, though, stamps `lastProgressAt` at the moment the chunk is emitted. `isCheckHeartbeatStalled` treated any timestamp ahead of the supplied `now` as an invalid heartbeat and failed closed, the same path used for null and garbage timestamps. Each new chunk therefore looked stalled until the next tick caught up, which is the show-and-hide cycle seen on the card.

The cancel route uses that same helper, so the allowance lives there rather than only in the Vue computed. Heartbeats up to fifteen seconds ahead of the observer clock count as idle zero. A minute ahead is still invalid, which keeps the existing fail-closed test and the cancel gate honest. The card also evaluates stall against the wall clock at compute time, with the interval tick only there to force a recompute, so a stale tick cannot manufacture a future heartbeat.

The second flap path is the snapshot. `refreshTaskChecks` replaced the in-memory run list with whatever `/api/tasks/:id/checks` returned. A poll in flight from before the latest chunk, or a payload whose `lastProgressAt` is null, wiped a beat the SSE handler had just recorded. The client now merges by run id and keeps the later valid timestamp. A running run that exists only on the SSE side is kept until the snapshot includes it. When every copy is old or missing, the merged heartbeat is still stalled, and `POST /api/tasks/:id/cancel-check` is unchanged: it still calls `isCheckHeartbeatStalled` on the server's own run.

The review history row drew a 3px inset bar on `.review-history-row.is-selected` while the first cell had `padding-left: 0`, so the bar covered `#8`. Both history tables share `.review-history-table`, so the first cell and header now have 12px of left padding on every row. Selection no longer shifts the other rows. The engineering-report round rows use the same selected class and the same bar, so the round number gets the same clearance.

## Approaches tried

A UI-only latch (show the button only after the threshold, hide it only after a much fresher beat) would have stopped boundary flicker, but it would have made the button disagree with the cancel route. The task asked for one rule. Hysteresis stayed out.

Ignoring future timestamps entirely would have hidden a real clock bug and weakened cancel. The fifteen-second window matches the slowest card tick and leaves the one-minute future case stalled.

Replacing the snapshot wholesale and only patching `lastProgressAt` when the client value was non-null was the first merge sketch. Keeping the newer of the two valid times also covers a snapshot that is merely older, not empty, which is what an in-flight poll looks like.

## Challenges and blockers

The button is driven by the card hint label `check stalled`, not by a separate drawer flag, so the drawer poll that refreshes remote activity was a false lead. That poll is already remote-only and does not replace check runs. The flap reproduced from the stall helper itself once `now` lagged the heartbeat.

The engineering-report table did not yet draw the inset bar; it only tinted the selected row. Sharing the review selected rule puts the bar on both, and the shared first-cell padding keeps the number readable in both.

## Key learnings

Fail-closed on a missing heartbeat is right for cancel. It is the wrong reading of a timestamp that is only ahead because the observer clock is the card's tick. Stall math has to allow a little skew or the button tracks the tick, not the check.

Two live copies of one run need an explicit merge. Last-write-wins between SSE and a polled snapshot will flicker any derived boolean that treats null as the bad state.
